latest.title: I Almost Shipped the Wrong Thing
latest.description: Agentic coding made shipping features almost free. Over two weeks, I shipped six on my Kanban project, and everyone worked. Then I realized I'd built a nicer Kanban board while the one feature that actually mattered sat untouched. This is about that failure mode: when code is cheap, velocity stops telling you whether you're on the right track. I share how I caught the drift and the memo-first workflow I now run before any agent writes code.

latest.title: When agents write the code, trust the evidence, not the approval
latest.description: When producing code is cheap, the scarce, risky step is confirming it does what was intended. A practical model for where to spend judgment and how to measure sign-off so it can't quietly become a rubber stamp.

latest.title: Serverless Is More Than Just a Technology
latest.description: Most engineers think of serverless as a way to simplify operations and improve scalability. While those benefits are real, serverless can also become a powerful business advantage. In this article, I share how we built Structor almost entirely on serverless AWS services, reduced our infrastructure costs to nearly zero, and gained the flexibility to compete on pricing against established players. Sometimes, the biggest benefit of serverless isn't technical, it's strategic.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.
